what_this_is: A6 homographs, settled. Three kinds of row, one file, because they are one decision: which record a lesson means when its headword names more than one, whether the sibling it does not mean is taught anywhere, and which siblings stay deliberately untaught. Every row carries the lesson's own words as its evidence; validate_repairs_applied.py replays all of them against the exported course tree on every run.

kinds.ref: One (headword, lesson) row of course/vocab_disambiguation_review.json. `old` is the slug the export carried before W11a, `new` the record the lesson actually means. `how: reading` = the lesson prints the kana beside the chip and scripts/export/vocab_identity.py derives it (the row asserts the rule still does; it is NOT fed back to the resolver). `how: ruling` = no reading is printed and the resolver cannot know, so the decision is loaded from here. W11c adds one row that never sat in that queue: only one record spells 様/よう there, so no queue row existed for the (headword, lesson) pair whose chip was nonetheless pointing at the wrong sibling.
kinds.unlock: One coverage_exemptions.json row promoted to a real unlock: the lesson named already teaches the word in prose, so it introduces it. `ref_written` is what both layers carry — a published slug since W11c retired the row-id form.
kinds.hold: A coverage exemption that STAYS, with the reason restated. The row is an assertion: the record must still be exempt and still unlocked by no lesson, so a hold cannot rot into a silent hole.
kinds.practice: One exercise authored so a promoted unlock is actually asked by its own lesson. validate_practice_coverage.py freezes the per-(level, kind) count of unlocked items no exercise targets and FAILS on growth, and it is right to: a card the SRS schedules and the lesson never rehearsed is the hole this unit is closing, not a new one to open. The exercise content lives here so the table is the source and the apply script is data-driven. 中/なか needed none: les:n5-comparacoes-02 already drills it through 〜の中で.

rows.why: Unlocking そば without asking about it would have grown validate_practice_coverage's (n5, vocab) debt, which is the regression that gate exists to catch: an unlock nobody drills is a card the SRS schedules and the lesson never rehearsed. The item reuses the lesson's own frame (lugar に + ser が + いる) and its own 犬, so it practises the new word and nothing else new.
rows.prompt: Diga em japonês, no registro casual, 'Tem um cachorro do meu lado.' (use 私, 側, に, 犬 e o verbo certo).

accept: わたしの側に犬がいる
わたしのそばに犬がいる

rows.explanation: Molde 〜の側に + [ser vivo] + が + いる. 側 (そば) é 'ao lado de, pertinho de', e o lugar da existência vem sempre marcado por に. Como 犬 é ser vivo, o verbo é いる, aqui na forma casual.

rows.why: Same reason. The lesson's interrogative list now teaches どなた with its own chip, so the practice asks for the word it just introduced.
rows.prompt: Complete a pergunta educada: ＿＿ですか。('Quem é o senhor / a senhora?')
rows.explanation: どなた é a forma educada de 誰 ('quem'). Vem do mesmo kanji de どちら, 何方: muda só a leitura. どちら pergunta 'qual dos dois' ou 'para onde'; どなた pergunta 'quem é'. Na recepção ou no telefone, どなたですか soa bem mais cortês do que 誰ですか.

rows.why: Same reason. The lesson already lists 何 as the word for asking 'por quê', and its subject is から, so the item asks the question that から answers.
rows.prompt: Complete a pergunta casual sobre o motivo: ＿＿で来なかったの？ ('Por que você não veio?')
rows.explanation: Aqui 何 se lê なん: 何で (なんで) é o 'por quê' mais casual, irmão de どうして. A resposta volta com から, como em 熱があったから ('porque eu estava com febre'). A leitura なん vem antes de sons das linhas た, だ e な (何で なんで, 何と なんと, 何の なんの, 何です なんです) e antes de contadores (何人 なんにん, 何時 なんじ). Antes de か, 何 continua なに: 何か se lê なにか.
rows.corrected: W11c: the last sentence said 何 'quase sempre vira なん' before で, か and と. Wrong for か — 何か is なにか. Restated with the rule that actually holds: なん before た/だ/な-row sounds and before counters, なに before か.

rows.why: Same reason. The lesson's own たら list conjugates 止めたら, so the item asks for the dictionary form behind it, which is also the transitivity contrast a learner needs here.
rows.prompt: A lição forma 止めたら a partir de qual forma de dicionário?
rows.explanation: たら sai do passado simples: 止める → 止めた → 止めたら. 止める (とめる) é o transitivo, o que age sobre algo: 車を止める, 音を止める ('parar o carro', 'desligar o som'). O par intransitivo é 止まる (とまる), quando algo para sozinho, e daria 止まったら.

exemption_headers.coverage: Records at taught levels that no lesson unlocks, each with the reason the gap is known and held rather than a silent regression. validate_unlock_ledger treats a taught-level record as a FAILURE unless it is unlocked exactly once or listed here; an entry matching nothing is also a failure, so this list cannot rot. W11a (owner decision A6) resolved five of the nine homograph placements into real unlocks; the four that remain are deferred with a stated reason and are re-asserted on every run by validate_repairs_applied.py against research/derived/repairs/homograph_rulings.json.
exemption_headers.gating: Item references a lesson BODY renders before the course unlocks them. validate_lesson_gating.py check B fails on any such reference unless it is listed here with the reason the gap is held rather than hidden; an entry that matches nothing is also a failure, so this list cannot rot. W11a closed four of the eight by unlocking the record its lesson already teaches. W11c closed a fifth by re-pointing the chip its lesson actually describes (様 @ les:n4-passiva-02, whose record the course unlocks a topic earlier). What remains is one forward reference and two homograph placements the owner deferred, which are also in course/coverage_exemptions.json.
